intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A world-renowned snorkeling spot set in a volcanic crater bay, perfect for families to explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish in calm, shallow waters. Kids and adults alike will be amazed by the marine life including sea turtles and colorful reef fish. Reservations are required in advance.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up a TheBus pass (cheapest public transit option, ~$3/ride or $70 monthly pass) and take Route 23 toward Hanauma Bay area. Check in to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a short walk to explore the neighborhood and nearby Maunalua Bay Beach Park — a calm, free beach perfect for a relaxed first afternoon dip.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront at sunset near Maunalua Bay. Head to Zippy's Restaurant (local Hawaii chain, budget-friendly plates $8–$14) for a classic local dinner — try the chili and rice or saimin noodle soup.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience snack on the bus (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Zippy's Restaurant — local Hawaiian comfort food, budget plates $8–$14

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at a local ABC Store or Walmart to save money throughout the trip. TheBus is the most budget-friendly way to get around Oahu — download the DaBus2 app for real-time routes.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — arrive by 7:00 AM to beat the crowds and secure entry (reservations required online, $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 12). Watch the mandatory 9-minute reef education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling among hundreds of tropical fish in the volcanic crater bay. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible to avoid rental fees (~$15 rental if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, walk or take a short bus ride to nearby Koko Head Crater Trail for a moderate hike up 1,048 railroad tie steps — completely free and offers breathtaking panoramic views of East Oahu, Hanauma Bay, and the Pacific Ocean. Great for families with older kids (allow 1–1.5 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rinse off and rest. Head to Koko Marina Center nearby for dinner at Poke Stop — fresh, affordable poke bowls starting at $12. Browse the marina area for free evening views of the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit and pastries from a nearby convenience store or prep simple breakfast at the hotel ($5–$8)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch with sandwiches and snacks from a local grocery store to eat near Hanauma Bay ($6–$10 per person)
meals.dinner: Poke Stop at Koko Marina Center — fresh poke bowls $12–$16

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are MANDATORY and slots fill up weeks in advance — book online at https://hanauma bay.hawaii.gov as soon as possible. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the coral.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, head to Sandy Beach Park (free, 5 minutes from hotel) — one of Oahu's most famous bodysurf and boogie board beaches. Watch the local bodyboarders tackle powerful shore break waves. Families with young children should stay in the calmer sections as the surf can be strong. Bring a frisbee or beach games for free fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus to Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free, ~45-minute round trip hike). The paved trail leads to stunning views of the Windward Coast, Rabbit Island, and Sea Life Park below. On clear days you may spot humpback whales (August is late season but possible). Afterward, visit Makapuu Beach Park for a swim — calmer conditions than Sandy Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the hotel and stop at Ono Seafood (a local favorite in nearby Hawaii Kai area) for affordable, fresh poke. Pick up groceries at Times Supermarket in Hawaii Kai for a budget-friendly breakfast prep for the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast at hotel — cereal, fruit, or toast purchased from grocery store ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or shave ice treat from a roadside stand near Sandy Beach ($5–$8)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — fresh poke plates $13–$17, or cook a simple meal at the hotel with groceries

day_by_day.notes: Sandy Beach has lifeguards but is known for strong shore break — supervise children closely. The Makapuu Lighthouse Trail is paved and stroller-accessible for most of its length, making it great for families.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus toward Waimanalo Beach — one of Oahu's longest and most beautiful white sand beaches, often less crowded than tourist hotspots. Spend the morning swimming, building sandcastles, and enjoying the stunning Koolau Mountain backdrop. Entry is free. Waimanalo Beach Park has restrooms, showers, and picnic tables.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Windward Coast to Kailua Beach Park (30 minutes by bus or car) — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. The calm, turquoise water is ideal for families. Rent kayaks to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (~$25–$35/hour for a double kayak) or simply relax on the white sand for free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua Town for dinner — a charming, walkable town with affordable local eateries. Try Kalapawai Market for fresh sandwiches and local plates ($10–$15) or Cinnamon's Restaurant for a casual dinner. Browse the boutique shops before taking the bus back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel with groceries purchased yesterday ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Waimanalo Beach — sandwiches and fruit ($6–$10)
meals.dinner: Kalapawai Market in Kailua Town — sandwiches, salads, and local plates $10–$15

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is about 30–40 minutes from the hotel by car or 45–60 minutes by bus. The bus ride itself is scenic and free with your pass. Waimanalo and Kailua are on the Windward side — mornings can be slightly cloudier but afternoons typically clear up beautifully.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples Memorial Park (~$5 entry per adult, $2 for children). This stunning replica of a 900-year-old Japanese temple sits against dramatic green cliffs and is surrounded by koi ponds and peacocks — a magical and affordable cultural experience for families. Spend 1–2 hours exploring the peaceful grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kualoa Regional Park (free beach park) on the Windward Coast — a breathtaking park with views of Chinaman's Hat island (Mokolii Island). The shallow, calm waters are perfect for young children. Bring snorkel gear to explore the shallow reef. Kualoa is also famous as a filming location for Jurassic Park, Lost, and many Hollywood movies.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the famous Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku (North Shore direction) for the iconic garlic butter shrimp plates (~$14–$16) — a must-try local experience. Eat at the picnic tables and enjoy the laid-back North Shore vibe before heading back south to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel with groceries ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Kualoa Regional Park — sandwiches and snacks ($6–$10)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku — garlic shrimp plates $14–$16 (cash only)

day_by_day.notes: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck is cash only — bring cash. Byodo-In Temple is a hidden gem that most tourists skip, making it a peaceful and memorable experience. Kualoa Regional Park has excellent picnic facilities and mountain views that are simply stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the North Shore — one of Hawaii's most iconic regions. Start at Sunset Beach (free) and walk the famous stretch of sand. In August, the summer swells are calm, making the water safe and ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Walk north to Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline) to see the famous surf break even in its calmer summer state.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town of the North Shore. Visit Matsumoto Shave Ice (~$4–$6) for the legendary rainbow shave ice, a Hawaii institution. Stroll the historic town, browse surf shops, and soak in the local culture. Visit Haleiwa Beach Park for a free afternoon swim in calm, protected waters perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens or grab affordable plate lunches from Haleiwa Eats food truck (~$10–$14). Take a scenic sunset drive back along Kamehameha Highway toward the hotel, stopping at any roadside fruit stands for fresh local produce.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local cafe in Haleiwa or pack from hotel ($5–$8)
meals.lunch: Roadside shrimp truck or plate lunch spot along Kamehameha Highway ($10–$14)
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Eats food truck or plate lunch restaurant in Haleiwa Town ($10–$14)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from East Oahu to the North Shore takes about 45–60 minutes by car. If using TheBus, take Route 55 from Kaneohe or plan a longer transit route — it's doable but takes 1.5–2 hours. Consider renting a car for this day for convenience (~$40–$60/day from budget rental companies).

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a second snorkeling session — if you loved it on Day 2, this is your chance to explore deeper sections of the bay or spend more time with the marine life. Alternatively, spend a relaxed morning at the hotel pool or nearby Maunalua Bay Beach Park for a free, low-key beach morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (~$5/person entry, or $10/vehicle). The iconic 1.6-mile round-trip hike takes about 1.5 hours and rewards hikers with panoramic views of Waikiki, Honolulu, and the Pacific Ocean. The trail involves some stairs and a tunnel — exciting for kids! Go in the afternoon for golden light photography.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Waikiki for the evening — explore the famous beachfront strip, watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly at sunset). Grab affordable dinner at a local spot away from the resort strip — try Marukame Udon in Waikiki for fresh udon noodles starting at $5–$9.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with groceries ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Diamond Head or grab a plate lunch near the trailhead ($8–$12)
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles $5–$9, budget-friendly and delicious

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations are recommended — book at https://gostateparks.hawaii.gov. The hike is moderately easy but involves stairs and a low tunnel — most children handle it well. Marukame Udon typically has a line but moves quickly and is one of the best budget meals in Waikiki.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Ala Moana Beach Park (free) — a massive, beautiful beach park adjacent to Ala Moana Center. The calm, protected lagoon is perfect for families with young children. Arrive early to claim a shaded picnic spot. Bring snorkel gear to explore the shallow reef near the Magic Island peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ala Moana Center — one of the world's largest open-air shopping malls. Even on a budget, it's worth exploring the food court (affordable local food options $8–$12) and the free cultural performances that often happen on weekends. Browse the Farmers Market if available. Then take a short walk or bus to Kakaako Waterfront Park for free street art murals (Pow! Wow! Hawaii) and ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Chinatown in downtown Honolulu for an affordable, authentic dinner. Try Little Village Noodle House ($10–$16 per dish, great for sharing) or browse the various Vietnamese, Chinese, and local restaurants. Chinatown is vibrant and colorful in the evening — a great cultural experience for families.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with groceries ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Center food court — local plate lunches, ramen, or poke bowls $8–$12
meals.dinner: Chinatown Honolulu — Little Village Noodle House or local Vietnamese/Chinese restaurants $10–$16 per dish

day_by_day.notes: Ala Moana Beach Park has excellent facilities including showers, restrooms, and lifeguards. The park is very popular on Sundays with local families — a great way to experience authentic Hawaiian local culture. Chinatown is generally safe in the evening but stay aware of your surroundings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (though timed entry passes are required — book in advance at recreation.gov). The Visitor Center and exhibits are free. Allow 2–3 hours for the full experience. This is an educational and memorable experience for older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, head to the nearby Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday only — if this falls on a different day, visit Pearlridge Center Mall instead for free browsing). Alternatively, visit the Bishop Museum (~$25/adult, $17/child) — Hawaii's premier natural history museum with fascinating exhibits on Hawaiian culture, volcanoes, and Pacific history. Look for discount coupons online.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the East Oahu area for a relaxed final full-day evening. Visit Koko Marina Center for shave ice at Island Vintage Shave Ice (~$7–$10) and a casual waterfront dinner at Kona Brewing Company (happy hour specials, appetizers $8–$14) or grab affordable takeout from a nearby local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before heading to Pearl Harbor ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Cafeteria at Pearl Harbor Visitor Center or packed lunch ($8–$12)
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina — happy hour specials and appetizers $8–$14, or local takeout

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry passes are FREE but must be reserved well in advance — book at recreation.gov as soon as possible as they fill up months ahead. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed at the memorial — leave large bags in the car or hotel. Children under 4 are not permitted on the USS Arizona Memorial boat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last sunrise walk at Maunalua Bay Beach Park or Sandy Beach (both free and steps from the hotel). Take a final swim in the warm Pacific waters and collect any last seashells. Pack a simple breakfast picnic to enjoy on the beach while watching the morning light over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head toward the airport (allow 30–45 minutes by car or 60–75 minutes by TheBus Route 23). Stop along the way at a local ABC Store or Times Supermarket to pick up affordable Hawaii souvenirs — macadamia nut chocolates, Kona coffee, and local snacks are great budget-friendly gifts. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Aloha and Mahalo! Reflect on 10 incredible days of beaches, snorkeling, hiking, and family memories in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final beach picnic breakfast — fruit, pastries, and juice from a grocery store ($5–$8)
meals.lunch: Grab a final local meal near the hotel before checkout — plate lunch from a local diner ($10–$14)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or inflight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with your hotel. TheBus to the airport runs regularly from the Hanauma Bay/Hawaii Kai area but allow extra time for luggage. Daniel K. Inouye International Airport has good food options post-security if you arrive early. Don't forget to use up any remaining bus passes or return rental cars before departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange ground transport to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay (~30–45 min drive from HNL).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the coastline near Hanauma Bay to get your bearings. Enjoy the ocean views and decompress from travel without overcommitting on Day 1.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Hawaii Kai for a relaxed welcome dinner. Explore the Hawaii Kai Town Center area for a casual first taste of local flavors.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before or after landing — try the local plate lunch options in the HNL terminal.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite near Hawaii Kai — try Zippy's for an affordable, iconic local chain serving saimin, chili rice, and plate lunches.
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company Hawaii Kai — mid-range waterfront dining with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and local craft beers with beautiful marina views.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may be a factor depending on origin. Purchase a snorkel gear rental or reserve a Hanauma Bay timed entry permit online tonight for Day 2 — they sell out fast and are required in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — arrive early (opens at 6:45 AM, reserve timed entry in advance). Watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling in the crystal-clear volcanic crater bay teeming with sea turtles, reef fish, and coral. Perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay to rinse off and rest. Spend the afternoon relaxing at the nearby beach or by the accommodation. Alternatively, drive 10 minutes to Sandy Beach Park to watch local bodyboarders — swimming here is for experienced swimmers only, but the scenery is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Kaimuki neighborhood (~20 min) for dinner — one of Oahu's best local dining neighborhoods with diverse, mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the boutique stay or pick up fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee from a nearby convenience store or farmers market.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Hanauma Bay — pack sandwiches, fruit, and snacks from a local grocery store (Times Supermarket in Hawaii Kai). No outside food/drink is technically allowed inside the preserve, so enjoy before or after.
meals.dinner: Mud Hen Water in Kaimuki — a beloved local restaurant celebrating Hawaiian cuisine with creative, seasonal dishes. Mid-range and family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay timed entry must be booked online in advance at hnl.info. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required), water shoes, and plenty of water. The bay is closed on Tuesdays for preservation.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, head to Waimanalo Beach — one of Oahu's most beautiful and uncrowded white-sand beaches, just 15 minutes from the boutique stay. Enjoy a peaceful family morning of swimming, sandcastle building, and beachcombing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Makapu'u Lighthouse Trail (~10 min from the boutique stay) for a moderate 2-mile paved round-trip hike with sweeping panoramic views of the Windward Coast, Rabbit Island, and (in season) humpback whale sightings. Great for families with older kids.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hawaii Kai or Kailua town (~25 min drive) for a casual evening dinner and ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — a beloved local breakfast spot famous for red velvet pancakes, eggs Benedict, and fresh-squeezed juice. Arrive early to beat the wait.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market & Deli in Kailua — a charming local market with made-to-order sandwiches, salads, and local snacks perfect for a beach or post-hike picnic.
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — a classic, mid-range family steakhouse and seafood restaurant with a casual, tropical atmosphere right across from Kailua Beach.

day_by_day.notes: Makapu'u Trail is paved and stroller/wheelchair accessible for most of the route. Bring hats and sunscreen — minimal shade. From November to May, this trail is also a prime whale-watching spot.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass — depart early from the boutique stay for the ~45-minute drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring the six Pacific island villages (Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Hawaii, Tahiti, Tonga), watching live cultural demonstrations, trying traditional crafts, and learning about Polynesian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon, a spectacular floating cultural show. Explore the IMAX theater and the Ali'i Luau (book in advance for the evening luau package if desired).
day_by_day.evening: Attend the 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a world-class Polynesian theatrical performance with fire knife dancing, music, and storytelling. Dinner is included with most evening packages.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay — prepare something simple or grab coffee and pastries to go before the drive.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with most day passes, offering a spread of Hawaiian and Polynesian-inspired dishes including kalua pork, poi, and fresh tropical fruit.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center (if booked as part of evening package) — traditional Hawaiian luau feast with imu-roasted pig, lomi salmon, haupia, and more. A memorable family experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center package online in advance — the Ambassador Package includes all-day access, the buffet lunch, reserved seating for the evening show, and the luau dinner, offering the best value. Plan for a full day — gates open at noon, evening show ends around 9:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour at Haleiwa Town — drive ~50 minutes from the boutique stay to Oahu's iconic North Shore surf town. Start with the legendary Matsumoto Shave Ice (arrive before the line gets long), then wander the charming main street browsing local boutiques, surf shops, and art galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Waimea Bay Beach Park (~10 min from Haleiwa) for an afternoon of swimming and relaxing on one of Oahu's most dramatic and beautiful beaches. In summer, the water is calm and ideal for families. Alternatively, visit nearby Shark's Cove for snorkeling (summer months only — calm conditions).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner in Haleiwa before the drive back to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — a beloved local breakfast spot serving famous breakfast burritos, kalua pork scrambles, and tropical smoothies at affordable prices.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck at Kahuku (~15 min from Haleiwa) — a legendary North Shore food truck institution serving garlic butter shrimp plates with rice. Cash-only and absolutely worth it.
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — a mid-range, casual waterfront restaurant in Haleiwa with fresh fish, burgers, and classic Hawaiian plates. Great views and family-friendly atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Haleiwa is a must-do North Shore experience. In summer, North Shore waves are small and calm — ideal for families. In winter (November–February), waves can be 20–30 feet and swimming is dangerous. Parking in Haleiwa town can be limited on weekends — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim — depart the boutique stay and drive ~45 minutes to Waimea Valley on the North Shore. Enjoy the gentle, paved 1.5-mile family-friendly walk through lush botanical gardens filled with tropical plants, peacocks, and cultural artifacts, culminating at the stunning 45-foot Waihi Falls where you can swim in the natural pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, drive back toward Honolulu and spend the afternoon at Ala Moana Beach Park (~40 min from Waimea Valley) — a large, calm, family-friendly beach with a protected lagoon, perfect for young swimmers. Browse the adjacent Ala Moana Center if shopping is of interest.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Waikiki for the evening — a classic Hawaii experience with beachfront ambiance, street performers, and diverse dining options.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the drive — pick up malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery in Honolulu if passing through, or prepare something at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Café on-site at Waimea Valley — a casual café offering sandwiches, salads, and light bites. Alternatively, pack a picnic lunch to enjoy in the botanical garden.
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — an extremely popular, affordable udon noodle restaurant with fresh, hand-pulled noodles and tempura. Expect a line but it moves quickly. Perfect for families on a mid-range budget.

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley charges a modest admission fee (~$20 adults, ~$10 children). Life jackets are provided for the waterfall swim. The path is paved and accessible for strollers. Bring water shoes and a towel for the waterfall pool.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a second snorkeling session — now that you know the layout, explore different sections of the reef and spend more time spotting marine life. This is a great opportunity for family members who want more time in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sea Life Park Hawaii (~5 min from the boutique stay) on the Windward Coast — a family-favorite marine park featuring dolphin encounters, penguin exhibits, sea turtle lagoons, and shark tank experiences. A fun, educational afternoon for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening near the boutique stay — enjoy a sunset walk along the coastline and a low-key dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the boutique stay — stock up on local fruits (papaya, pineapple, mango), granola, and yogurt from Times Supermarket in Hawaii Kai.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near Hanauma Bay — pack sandwiches, chips, and local snacks. Enjoy on the grassy area outside the preserve after snorkeling.
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kaimuki (~20 min) — a no-frills, cash-only local institution serving authentic Hawaiian plate lunches including laulau, kalua pig, poi, and haupia. Very affordable and a true local experience.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park admission is approximately $40–$50 per adult and $25–$35 per child. Dolphin and animal interaction experiences cost extra and should be booked in advance. Saturday can be busy — arrive early to both Hanauma Bay and Sea Life Park.

day_by_day.morning: Diamond Head State Monument Hike — drive ~25 minutes to the iconic Diamond Head crater. The 1.6-mile round-trip hike to the summit offers breathtaking 360-degree views of Waikiki, Honolulu, and the Pacific Ocean. Moderately strenuous with some stairs and tunnels — great for families with kids 6 and up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for an afternoon of classic Hawaii beach time — rent surfboards or take a beginner surf lesson from one of the many beachfront surf schools. This is a bucket-list family activity and Waikiki's gentle waves are perfect for first-timers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special evening in Waikiki — watch the sunset from the beach and splurge slightly on a memorable dinner at a beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Café near Diamond Head — a popular local breakfast spot with acai bowls, omelets, fresh-squeezed juice, and coffee. Great fuel before the hike.
meals.lunch: The Pig and the Lady in Chinatown (~30 min) or grab casual poke bowls from Foodland Farms in Ala Moana — fresh, customizable poke bowls at excellent value.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki at the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort — a mid-range, iconic beachfront restaurant named after legendary surfer Duke Kahanamoku. Fresh fish, burgers, hula pie dessert, and live Hawaiian music. A quintessential Waikiki experience.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance timed-entry reservations at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen — the hike has minimal shade. Surf lessons in Waikiki run approximately $30–$50 per person for a group lesson (1.5–2 hours). Book in advance on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum (~30 min from the boutique stay) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum with world-class exhibits on Hawaiian and Pacific Island culture, a planetarium, and interactive science exhibits. Educational and engaging for families of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kailua Beach Park on the Windward Coast (~15 min from the boutique stay) — consistently ranked among the best beaches in the United States. The powdery white sand and calm turquoise waters are ideal for swimming, kayaking, and paddleboarding. Rent equipment from local vendors near the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Kailua-Hawaii Kai area — enjoy a relaxed dinner celebrating your last full day.

meals.breakfast: Moke's Bread & Breakfast in Kailua — a beloved local spot famous for their lilikoi (passion fruit) pancakes, loco moco, and fresh-baked goods. Arrive early — expect a wait on weekends.
meals.lunch: Kailua Town has excellent lunch options — try Kalapawai Café & Deli for fresh sandwiches and salads, or Cactus Mexican Grille for casual Mexican-Hawaiian fusion at mid-range prices.
meals.dinner: Assaggio Italian Restaurant in Kailua — a local favorite for mid-range Italian food with generous portions, fresh pasta, and seafood. Family-friendly and consistently excellent.

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is open daily and admission is approximately $25 adults / $17 children. Allow 2–3 hours. Kailua Beach kayak and paddleboard rentals run approximately $20–$30 per hour. The beach can get busy on weekends — arrive by mid-morning for the best parking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, relaxed start. Take one last walk along the coastline near Hanauma Bay at sunrise, collect shells, and soak in the final views of the Pacific. Pack up and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, stop at Ala Moana Center for last-minute souvenir shopping — Hawaii's largest open-air mall with everything from local brands (Sig Zane, Manaola) to mainstream stores. Pick up local treats: Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt, and local chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Honolulu International Airport (HNL) — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights. Reflect on an incredible 10 days in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: One last breakfast at a local favorite — try Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center (~20 min away) for creative breakfast plates, or enjoy a simple breakfast at the boutique stay using leftover groceries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ala Moana Center — Makai Market Food Court offers diverse, affordable options including poke, plate lunches, ramen, and local desserts. A great final taste of Hawaii's food diversity.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at HNL — try Makai Market or local options in the terminal. Alternatively, if time allows before heading to the airport, enjoy a final sit-down meal at a nearby restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the boutique stay. Store luggage at the hotel if needed while finishing last-minute activities. Ala Moana Center is open from 9:30 AM. For international departures, arrive at HNL at least 3 hours early. Don't forget to declare any agricultural items (fresh fruit, flowers, etc.) — many cannot be taken off the islands.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A world-renowned snorkeling spot set in a volcanic crater bay, perfect for families to explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish in calm, shallow waters. Kids and adults alike will be amazed by the marine life including sea turtles and colorful reef fish. Reservations are required in advance.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass
experiences.description: An immersive family cultural experience showcasing the traditions, music, dance, and food of six Polynesian island nations including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Includes canoe rides, live performances, and a spectacular evening luau show that kids absolutely love.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: A gentle, paved 1.5-mile family-friendly hike through a lush botanical garden leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Families can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall with lifeguards on duty. The trail is stroller-friendly and features peacocks and tropical plants along the way.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of Hawaii's most iconic and family-friendly beaches on Maui. The calm, clear waters are ideal for swimming, boogie boarding, and building sandcastles. Rent snorkel gear to spot sea turtles near Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), and enjoy beachside dining at nearby restaurants along the strip.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour at Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore and indulge in Hawaii's most beloved treat — rainbow shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's. Sample local plate lunches, fresh poke bowls, and malasadas from roadside stands and local eateries. A delicious and affordable cultural food experience the whole family will enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay via private luxury car service (~30–40 min drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique property, unpack, and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll along the coastline near Hanauma Bay to get your first taste of the stunning East Oahu scenery. Enjoy a welcome amenity and refresh with tropical drinks arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace or private lanai overlooking the Pacific. Ease into vacation mode with a relaxed first dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or light snack upon arrival at hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roy's Hawaii Kai — an iconic East Oahu fine-dining institution by Chef Roy Yamaguchi, offering Hawaiian Fusion cuisine with fresh island seafood, just minutes from the hotel. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag may be a factor especially for families traveling from the mainland or internationally.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — Start early (gates open at 6:45 AM) to beat crowds and secure parking. All visitors must watch a mandatory 9-minute marine education video before entering. Explore the vibrant coral reef ecosystem teeming with tropical fish right from the hotel's backyard. Rent premium snorkel gear on-site or bring your own. Perfect for families — the inner bay is shallow and calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch and rest. In the early afternoon, drive the scenic Makapuu Lighthouse Trail (approx. 15 min from hotel) — a paved, 2-mile round-trip coastal walk with panoramic ocean views and whale watching potential (note: peak whale season is Dec–April, but spinner dolphins are common year-round).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Makapuu Beach Park followed by a premium dinner back near Hawaii Kai.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or hotel breakfast spread — fresh tropical fruits, acai bowls, Kona coffee, and pastries
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled fish tacos, fresh poke bowls, and fresh-squeezed lilikoi lemonade
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company Hawaii Kai — relaxed upscale dining with craft beers, fresh seafood, and gorgeous marina views; family-friendly with a sophisticated atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are REQUIRED and must be booked online in advance (up to 2 days before). Arrive at opening time for the best marine life experience and cooler temperatures. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore of Oahu (~1 hour from hotel). Begin with a visit to Waimea Valley — a lush 1,875-acre botanical garden and cultural heritage site. Enjoy the gentle, paved 1.5-mile family-friendly hike through incredible tropical flora leading to the breathtaking 45-foot Waimea Falls waterfall. Swim in the natural pool at the base of the falls (life jackets provided). Guides are available for cultural storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Haleiwa Town for the famous Shave Ice and Local Food Tour — explore the charming surf village on the North Shore, stopping at legendary Matsumoto Shave Ice for rainbow shave ice with mochi and azuki beans. Browse local boutiques, art galleries, and surf shops. Sample garlic shrimp from the iconic Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, fresh banana bread, and local tropical fruit stands.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely sunset drive back along the Kamehameha Highway hugging the coastline. Dinner in Haleiwa or back in East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — Eggs Benedict with lomi lomi salmon, fresh papaya, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Haleiwa Local Food Tour — Giovanni's Shrimp Truck garlic shrimp plates, fresh poke from Haleiwa Bowls, and shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — a beloved North Shore institution with fresh catch of the day, prime steaks, and stunning garden views; upscale casual with a warm island vibe

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley opens at 9:00 AM. Bring water shoes for the waterfall pool swim. The North Shore road can be narrow — consider a luxury SUV rental for comfort. August is summer in Hawaii so the North Shore surf is typically calm and ideal for families (big wave season is Nov–Feb).

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass — Drive ~45 minutes from the hotel to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Arrive at opening (11:00 AM) to maximize time across all six Polynesian village experiences representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations — fire-making, weaving, hula, and traditional games. Ideal for families with children of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon (typically at 2:30 PM), a colorful parade of traditional watercraft and performances. Explore the IMAX theater showing Hawaiian cultural films. Enjoy a traditional Hawaiian luau feast (included with premium passes).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous HA: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production with fire dancing, acrobatics, and Polynesian storytelling. One of Hawaii's most celebrated live performances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Loco Moco (Hawaiian comfort classic: rice, hamburger patty, fried egg, and gravy), fresh tropical juice
meals.lunch: Light snacks and tropical drinks within the Polynesian Cultural Center villages
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an all-you-can-eat traditional Hawaiian luau buffet featuring kalua pig, poi, haupia, fresh fish, and tropical desserts; included with Gateway or Ali'i Luau package

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ali'i Luau + HA Show package in advance — premium seating sells out quickly, especially in August. The full day runs approximately 11:00 AM to 9:30 PM. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a light layer for the evening show in the open-air theater.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury relaxation day — Start with a private sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged through the hotel. Follow with a world-class spa morning at a nearby luxury spa (Spa Olakino at Turtle Bay Resort, ~1 hour north, or arrange in-hotel treatments). Choose from traditional lomilomi massage, hot stone therapy, or family wellness treatments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hanauma Bay area for a private catamaran sailing charter — depart from Hawaii Kai Marina for a 2–3 hour luxury sail along the stunning East Oahu coastline. Look for sea turtles, dolphins, and vibrant coastal cliffs. Premium charters include snorkeling stops, champagne, and gourmet appetizers on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the boutique property — arrange a private in-room or lanai dining experience catered by a local private chef specializing in Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-room luxury breakfast — smoked salmon Benedict, fresh fruit platter, granola with local honey, and Kona pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: On the catamaran — gourmet charcuterie, fresh sushi, tropical fruit, and premium beverages
meals.dinner: Private chef experience at the boutique stay — a curated 4-course Hawaiian tasting menu featuring fresh catch, locally grown vegetables, and a lilikoi cheesecake dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter at least 1 week in advance through companies like Honolulu Sailing Co. or Magic Sail Charters. Private chef services can be arranged through platforms like Take a Chef or via the hotel concierge. This is an ideal rest and rejuvenation day mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Diamond Head Crater Hike — Drive ~20 minutes west to the iconic Diamond Head State Monument. Hike the 1.6-mile round-trip trail (moderate, partially paved) to the summit for sweeping 360-degree views of Honolulu, Waikiki, and the Pacific Ocean. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to avoid midday heat. Reservations required online.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Waikiki Beach — just 5 minutes from Diamond Head. Arrange a private surf lesson for the family through Hans Hedemann Surf School (one of Hawaii's most prestigious surf schools). After lessons, relax on the iconic beach with reserved beach chairs and umbrella service. Browse luxury boutiques along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Upscale dinner in Waikiki followed by a stroll along the illuminated beachfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the hotel — acai smoothie bowls, hard-boiled eggs, banana, and granola bars to go
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at The Veranda at Moana Surfrider — elegant open-air dining at Hawaii's first hotel with fresh salads, lobster rolls, and ocean views right on Waikiki Beach
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu at the Nobu Hotel — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion by Chef Nobu Matsuhisa; signature dishes include black cod miso and yellowtail jalapeño; sophisticated and family-welcoming

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations must be made at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Arrive at the trailhead by 7:00 AM for cooler temps and fewer crowds. Bring water and sun protection. Waikiki parking can be challenging — use a rideshare or taxi from Diamond Head.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui — Book an early morning Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines flight from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului (OGG), approximately 35 minutes. Arrange a luxury SUV rental upon arrival. Check in to a premium Kaanapali Beach resort (suggested: Hyatt Regency Maui, Westin Kaanapali, or Andaz Maui at Wailea for ultra-luxury).
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Beach Day — Spend the afternoon at one of Hawaii's most celebrated beaches. The calm, crystal-clear waters are perfect for swimming, snorkeling with sea turtles, and paddleboarding. Rent premium water sports equipment through the resort. Explore Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) — a lava rock promontory famous for snorkeling and cliff diving.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary torch lighting and cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a Kaanapali tradition performed nightly at the Sheraton Maui. Dinner at a premier Kaanapali restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or airport lounge before departure — continental spread with fresh fruit and pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach, Kaanapali — iconic oceanfront dining with fresh fish tacos, poke bowls, and tropical cocktails with your toes in the sand
meals.dinner: Japengo at the Hyatt Regency Maui — award-winning Pacific Rim cuisine with sushi, fresh seafood, and stunning ocean views; one of Maui's finest dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2 weeks in advance. Kaanapali Beach is on Maui's West Shore — a different island requiring a short flight. Arrange resort accommodations in advance as August is peak season. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony is free and open to all beach guests.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakala National Park — Wake at 3:00 AM for the drive to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 ft elevation). Watch the awe-inspiring sunrise above the clouds — one of the most magical experiences in all of Hawaii. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to 40°F. Reservations required for the sunrise viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and explore Upcountry Maui — stop at Surfing Goat Dairy for a family farm tour and artisan goat cheese tasting, and Ali'i Kula Lavender Farm for stunning views and lavender products. Drive the scenic back road through Makawao town for local art galleries and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali for a relaxing evening. Sunset cocktails at the resort pool bar.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed sunrise snack box arranged by the resort — thermos of hot Kona coffee, warm pastries, and fresh fruit to enjoy at the Haleakala summit
meals.lunch: Upcountry Maui lunch at Hali'imaile General Store — a legendary Maui institution by Chef Bev Gannon set in a historic pineapple plantation building; famous for fresh island cuisine and creative cocktails
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui, Kapalua — farm-to-table fine dining by James Beard-nominated Chef Peter Merriman with panoramic ocean views; locally sourced ingredients and exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked at recreation.gov — they sell out weeks in advance. Bring extremely warm layers — the temperature difference from the beach to the summit is dramatic. The drive from Kaanapali to the summit takes approximately 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — Depart early for the iconic Road to Hana, one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Stop at Twin Falls for a short waterfall hike, Garden of Eden Arboretum for lush tropical gardens and dramatic ocean overlooks, and Wailua Falls — one of Maui's most photogenic waterfalls. Take your time and enjoy the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hana Town and beyond to Ohe'o Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools) in Kipahulu District of Haleakala National Park — swim in the natural tiered freshwater pools surrounded by waterfalls and lush rainforest. Explore the Pipiwai Trail to the 400-foot Waimoku Falls through a stunning bamboo forest.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive along the Road to Hana (or continue around the south shore of Maui for a full loop — add ~1 hour). Arrive back at Kaanapali for a late, leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — loco moco, fresh tropical fruit, and strong Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stops along the Road to Hana — banana bread from the famous Aunty Sandy's in Keanae, fresh coconut water, and tropical fruit from roadside stands
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill, Lahaina — one of Maui's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants; award-winning New American cuisine with macadamia nut-crusted fish, prime beef, and an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles but takes 3–4 hours one way due to 620 curves and 59 bridges. Start by 7:00 AM to maximize daylight. Ohe'o Gulch requires a National Parks pass. Bring snacks, water, and motion sickness remedies if needed for young children. The road is narrow — drive carefully and use pullouts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Kaanapali Beach — Enjoy a last leisurely swim and paddleboard session on the iconic beach. Treat the family to a premium snorkeling excursion from the beach — Black Rock offers excellent coral and sea turtle encounters just offshore. Soak in the last moments of the turquoise Pacific.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Maui resort. Arrange a luxury airport transfer to Kahului Airport (OGG). Depending on departure time, stop at the Shops at Wailea for last-minute luxury shopping — Tiffany & Co., Louis Vuitton, and local Hawaiian jewelry and art galleries. Pick up premium Hawaiian gifts: Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, Hawaiian sea salt, and local artwork.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight from Maui (OGG) or return inter-island flight to Honolulu (HNL) for international connections. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final luxury hotel breakfast — a celebratory spread of eggs your way, fresh tropical fruit, acai bowls, macadamia nut pancakes with coconut syrup, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman, Wailea — beloved Maui gathering place with fresh island fare, handcrafted cocktails, and live Hawaiian music; perfect final Maui meal
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight — or if time allows, a final dinner at Amasia at Grand Wailea (Forbes Five-Star resort) for a spectacular send-off meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — request late checkout if your flight departs in the evening. Allow extra time at Kahului Airport during summer peak season. Consider shipping home any fragile purchases or oversized souvenirs. Confirm all return flight details and arrange luggage assistance through the resort concierge.
